params.body:
## Why

`main` was red: five failures in `Tests\Feature\VinLookupMessageTest`, all "Failed asserting
that 302 is identical to 200". Two pull requests were green on their own branch and red
together.

PR 269 made `App\Http\Middleware\Access` stop skipping its check for a session without
`MT_ACCESS`: the rights are rebuilt from the database for the logged-in user and the normal
check runs on them. PR 270 added the VIN message tests, and they authenticate with
`actingAs()` only. `actingAs()` gives a user, not a session: no `MT_ACCESS`, and the role the
test creates has no rows in `role_access`, so the rebuilt rights hold `home` and `import` and
nothing else. Every request to `ownvehicle.*` is therefore redirected to `home.index`.

The middleware is right and the tests were wrong: a real dealer never reaches those screens
without rights either.

## What

`tests/TestCase.php` gets `actingAsWithRights($user, ...$menus)`, which logs a user in the
way `LoginController@authenticated` does: authenticated **and** with the rights in the
session under `MT_ACCESS`, built from `App\Support\AccessRights::forUser()` plus the menus
the test needs. There was no shared helper for this (every test that needed rights spelled
out its own `MT_ACCESS` array), so the next test could have repeated the mistake; now it has
one call to make. `loginRights()` sits next to it for a test that wants the array only.

`VinLookupMessageTest` uses it with the `ownvehicle` menu, which is the security key of both
routes it exercises (`ownvehicle.create.fromCarVwe` and `ownvehicle.create`).

No application code is touched.

## Which tests were wrong

Only `VinLookupMessageTest` (five tests). The full suite was then read for every other test
that authenticates without rights. Sixteen files do, all green, and all for a reason that is
not luck:

- Explicitly without the middleware: `DealerAuthorizationTest`, `UserAuthorizationTest`,
  `OfferToOrderTest`, `OrderCreateTest`, `RowActionsOwnershipTest`, `VehicleProposalTest`
  (`withoutMiddleware()`), `CarpassPasswordTest` (`withoutMiddleware(Access::class)`).
- A Livewire component tested directly, so no HTTP middleware runs: `AveragePriceSearchTest`,
  `StocklistBrowserTest`, `VehicleFormSaveTest`, `VehicleSheetOptionOrderTest`.
- No HTTP request at all, only a repository or a model: `VehicleFilterInjectionTest`,
  `VehiclePriceLogicTest`.
- Routes the middleware is not on: `PartnerApiTest` (the Passport API), `MollieWebhookTest`
  (the webhook).
- `VehicleListTest` has one such request, `get('/own-vehicles')`, but that test is
  `markTestSkipped` for an unrelated order-dependency.

None of them were changed: they pass because their route does not reach the check, not
because they carry rights, and rewriting them would be churn.

## Whether any real path regressed

No. Checked against local MySQL with a throwaway test that logs in through the real login
route (`POST /login`) as a dealer whose role has rights rows in `menus` / `role_access`:

| path | status |
| --- | --- |
| `/own-vehicles` | 200 |
| `/own-vehicles/create` (the vehicle sheet) | 200 |
| `/exports` | 200 |
| `/settings` | 200 |

And the same four for the other half of 269, an authenticated session that never carried
`MT_ACCESS` (a remember-me cookie, a session that lost its data): 200 as well, with the rights
rebuilt from the database. That case used to pass the middleware unchecked and render with
undefined variables. The one behaviour that did change is the intended one: a user whose role
has no right on a menu is now redirected instead of let through.

## Checked

- `php artisan test` (full suite) against local MySQL, database `test`, schema from
  `database/schema/mysql-schema.sql` plus the post-2026-07-28 migrations, as the CI does.
- Before: 5 failed (`VinLookupMessageTest`) plus `BuildStampTest`. After: only
  `BuildStampTest`, which fails inside a git worktree by design.
- `VinLookupMessageTest` on its own: 5 passed, 28 assertions.
params.title: Tests: green main again after the access change
